extracted.intended_audience: Council on Environmental Quality (CEQ), federal agency NEPA practitioners, permit applicants/project proponents (especially electric industry), and NEPA counsel
extracted.subtask_short: NEPA rule comments for energy sector
extracted.subtask_description: Public-comment recommendations on CEQ's Proposed NEPA Rule and Draft GHG Guidance focused on improving efficiency, clarity, and legal defensibility of NEPA reviews for energy infrastructure projects. Covers procedural changes (scoping, CEs, tiering, alternatives, joint decisions) and guidance for GHG analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEPA procedural requirements (what a statement must address)
rubrics_metrics.description: NEPA requires preparation of a statement on: (i) the environmental impact of the proposed action, (ii) any adverse environmental effects which cannot be avoided should the proposal be implemented, (iii) alternatives to the proposed action, (iv) the relationship between local short-term uses of man’s environment and the maintenance and enhancement of long-term productivity, and (v) any irreversible and irretrievable commitments of resources which would be involved in the proposed action should it be implemented. (42 U.S.C. § 4332(2)(C))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statutory list frames the scope of NEPA reviews; regulatory changes should facilitate efficient compliance with these procedural obligations while preserving NEPA’s goal of informing the public and agency decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide flexibility to allow project proponents to assist in preparation and participate in scoping
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ proposes allowing project proponents and contractors to assume a greater role in preparing environmental documents and to participate in scoping earlier (including before publication of an NOI) under proposed §§1501.9 and 1506.5(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early participation by proponents/consultants can supply critical technical, environmental, and engineering information, produce a more robust record, improve communication with agencies, enable more meaningful public comment, and lead to higher-quality and more timely NEPA documents. Agencies must, however, retain responsibility to independently evaluate and take responsibility for documents prepared with proponent participation. Public comment processes and rigorous review remain required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage coordination between agency-selected NEPA contractors and project proponents
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibition on coordination between lead-agency contractors and non-federal applicants before permit submission can cause delays, higher costs, and inaccuracies in preliminary drafts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ should consider ways to encourage coordination so contractors can obtain timely, accurate, and relevant information from proponents, thereby reducing lags, preparation costs, and errors in draft NEPA documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify and expand appropriate use of Categorical Exclusions (CEs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies can categorically exclude actions that normally would not have significant effects; CEs are subject to their own NEPA analyses, public notice and comment, and CEQ review (see 40 C.F.R. §1508.4 and §1507.3(a)). CEQ proposes new regulatory text (e.g., proposed §1501.4, §1506.3(f), §1507.3(e)(5)) to provide clarity on CE use and extraordinary circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final regulations should codify clarity on extraordinary circumstances (the presence of such circumstances does not automatically preclude CE use; agencies should consider whether mitigation allows CE use). CE expansion avenues (adopting another agency's CE determination for substantially similar actions and importing wholesale another agency’s CE into one’s procedures) should be finalized. CEs are not exemptions from NEPA and must be well substantiated and consistent with reasoned agency decision-making. Cross-references between related sections (e.g., §1506.3(f) and §1507.3) would clarify authority and avoid duplicative EAs/EISs when another agency already determined no significant effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow agencies to adopt another agency’s CE determination when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §1506.3(f) would allow an agency to adopt another agency’s determination that a CE applies if the adopting agency’s proposed action is substantially the same; proposed §1507.3(e)(5) allows wholesale import of another agency's CE into one’s NEPA procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This authority would reduce duplication, save taxpayer resources, and is particularly useful where expert agencies within a department (e.g., DOI entities) would otherwise repeat analyses already done by peers. CEQ should finalize these provisions and encourage agency adoption of others’ CEs where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permit and encourage tiering and incorporation by reference of prior analyses (proposed §§1501.11 & 1501.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should be able to use existing studies and environmental analyses (tiering) and incorporate relevant earlier studies by reference to build upon prior work without requiring new processes or materials that add no substantive information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tiering and incorporation minimize duplication, ensure lead agencies utilize the most appropriate subject-matter information, and improve efficiency. CEQ should finalize the proposed changes and consider providing additional guidance on how to appropriately tier from previous studies and possibly create a repository/library of studies accessible to agencies and proponents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify scope and reasonableness standard for alternatives analysis (proposed §1502.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Proposed Rule clarifies that NEPA does not mandate a specific set or number of alternatives; agencies must analyze 'reasonable' but not exhaustive alternatives. Reasonableness is judged by the nature of the underlying agency action; alternatives analyses must provide sufficient information to permit a reasoned choice of alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When agencies review authorizations, purpose-and-need statements (and resulting alternatives) should be based on both the applicant’s goals and the agency’s statutory authority. The rule should avoid prescribing a maximum number of alternatives or otherwise constraining consideration of actual and feasible alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt and build on the One Federal Decision framework / require joint documents when practicable
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ proposes codifying One Federal Decision by requiring agencies to prepare joint EISs/Records of Decision and EAs/FONSIs when practicable and by codifying lead and cooperating agency designations (proposed §1500.6 and §1501.7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formalizing joint decisions promotes earlier coordination, reduces duplicative and inconsistent reviews, leverages expertise across agencies, and speeds project implementation. CEQ should finalize these changes, while recognizing initial coordination challenges (e.g., for FONSIs) that may lessen with experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow cooperation with state, tribal, and local environmental documents to avoid duplication (proposed §1506.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed revision to §1506.2 acknowledges increasing numbers of state/tribal/local environmental documents and allows federal agencies to cooperate so that one document will comply with NEPA and applicable state/tribal/local requirements, where not in conflict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adoption or cooperation with robust state-level documentation can increase efficiency in NEPA processes and reduce inconsistent outcomes; CEQ should finalize these changes and consider whether federal adoption of state documents under §1506.3 is feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require reasonable, contextualized consideration and quantification of GHG emissions
rubrics_metrics.description: GHG emissions are relevant to NEPA analyses and, where appropriate, federal agencies should take reasonable steps to quantify GHG emissions and place such quantifications in context and with caveats. CEQ’s proposed clarification of 'effects' and its emphasis on a 'reasonableness' standard is appropriate, but indirect and cumulative effects—including GHGs—may need assessment in particular circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ should provide general guidance to agencies on when and how to approach indirect and cumulative GHG impacts, encourage use of existing emissions estimates (including sector-wide estimates), quantify emissions when they are substantial, and require well-reasoned explanations for analyses to withstand judicial review. Guidance and examples on how to assess significance for NEPA purposes would be helpful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use sector-wide GHG analyses to provide context when project-level quantification is difficult
rubrics_metrics.description: Because GHGs are well-mixed pollutants and project-specific effects on global warming are difficult to predict precisely, sector-wide assessments (e.g., power sector trends) can help contextualize a project's direct, indirect, and cumulative emissions impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ should make clear that sector-wide assessments are appropriate and can be submitted by project proponents; agencies should consider such analyses to support qualitative assessments when project-specific quantification is infeasible. Reliable sources (e.g., EIA) and sector trends can demonstrate whether projects may reduce or increase net emissions (e.g., enabling renewables integration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid speculative emissions analyses and ensure GHG analyses do not improperly drive decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should balance NEPA’s information disclosure requirements with the inherent difficulties of quantifying reasonably foreseeable direct and indirect GHG emissions; speculative analyses may be legally and practically problematic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ's guidance should discourage highly speculative emissions quantification, make clear that GHG emissions alone should not drive federal decision-making, and encourage analyses that are proportionate, well-reasoned, and contextualized so projects can withstand judicial scrutiny without unnecessary delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure NEPA analyses are legally defensible and help projects avoid litigation delays
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory changes and guidance should help agencies produce NEPA analyses that satisfy judicial precedents finding failures to consider or quantify GHG emissions can violate NEPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ’s final rule or subsequent guidance should provide general approaches, examples, and references to applicable court decisions so agencies can navigate fact-specific judicial requirements, use appropriate methods (including existing sector estimates), and reduce the risk of remands or litigation-related permitting delays that create investor uncertainty for critical infrastructure projects.
